header: Date: 2026-05-17 | Time: 10:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Singh, Jamal Ortiz (Redwood); Mark Rivera, Dana Liu, Omar Khan, Ellen Park (BlueWave)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on last night's reliability incidents: intermittent 5xx errors and timeouts observed during mid-day traffic spike. Team reviewed preliminary root cause hypotheses (autoscale lag + upstream throttling), agreed on logs/metrics to correlate, prioritized live debug session, and set actions for Dedicated pilot pricing and security docs. Agreed plan: replicate spike in test environment, run controlled load with current autoscaling settings, and validate retry/backoff and rate-limit behavior.
topics: Preliminary root cause hypotheses (autoscaler, rate-limits, KV cache eviction)
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for reliability
transcript:
00:00 Alex Kim: ok everyone good morning, uh thanks for joining, this is our weekly POC sync, main agenda is follow-up on the reliability incident last night, quick intros
00:12 Mark Rivera: hey Mark here SRE at BlueWave, we saw a bunch of 5xxs around 02:10 UTC and some client timeouts, impact to a subset of our users
00:22 Priya Singh: Priya from Redwood SE, thanks Mark, i've pulled initial traces, looks like a spike in request tail latencies and some upstream 503s
00:35 Dana Liu: Dana, product, just to reiterate impact - a few queued jobs failed and some clinicians saw errors when saving notes
00:45 Alex Kim: ok thanks, quick recap of timeline from your side Mark?
00:50 Mark Rivera: timeline, roughly 01:55 to 02:20 we saw p95 jump from 120ms to 1.8s and p99 hit 3.5s, 5xxs concentrated on the generation endpoint, also some 429s earlier
01:10 Priya Singh: interesting, 429s then 5xxs could indicate upstream throttling, or our autoscaler couldn't add pods fast enough but some requests were already queued at the load balancer
01:25 Ellen Park: we did roll a small ingress change 01:10 UTC but not sure it aligns, i'll pull the change log
01:35 Jamal Ortiz: (Redwood CSM) noted, thanks Ellen
01:40 Alex Kim: hypothesis A: autoscale lag + cold startup on model workers causing timeouts and downstream 5xx cascades, hypothesis B: upstream rate-limiter (third party) returning 429 which our client then retried aggressively causing a circuit-breaker trip
02:00 Mark Rivera: also saw memory pressure and a couple of OOM kill logs on one node around 02:05
02:10 Priya Singh: that could explain KV cache evictions - if KV cache is dropped we pay warmup penalty, also we saw a few 'KV cache miss' patterns in the traces (auto transcript: K V spelled out)
02:30 Dana Liu: how would this change if we were on Dedicated? less noisy neighbors?
02:38 Alex Kim: yes Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and predictable throughput, fewer noisy neighbor issues and faster scale because reserved capacity can warm workers faster; but that comes with commit pricing - i'll send the numbers
02:55 Priya Singh: for hosted we have autoscaling params that we can tune: scale up threshold, target CPU, and burst capacity - we suspect the current target is too conservative for your traffic pattern
03:10 Mark Rivera: the rate limits we saw were at the third-party embedding service, not Redwood, but the way retries are configured on the client side made the spike worse
03:25 Priya Singh: right, we recommend exponential backoff with jitter and limiting overall retry attempts; we can push a client-side change in your test env
03:40 Ellen Park: also curious about timeouts, our front end has a 2s timeout - should we increase?
03:50 Priya Singh: careful there, increasing client timeouts can hide issues; better to fix root cause, but for short term increasing to 5s for specific routes plus better retry would reduce user-visible errors
04:10 Dana Liu: on observability, can you share a breakdown of token-level cost and per-route latency so we can correlate cost vs risk?
04:20 Alex Kim: yes i'll share the benchmark sheet and cost breakdown, link in chat: /docs/benchmarks/reliability-2026-05-17.xlsx (note: internal link)
04:35 Mark Rivera: can you also share the raw error logs and autoscaler event traces?
04:40 Priya Singh: will do, i'll redact any PII, attach stack traces and the request ids
04:50 Alex Kim: security asks - Dana had wanted SOC2 and KMS details for Dedicated pilot
04:55 Dana Liu: yes, need SOC2 report summary and KMS/HSM info for encryption at rest
05:05 Alex Kim: i'll send SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes, also the audit log format, and a short doc comparing Hosted vs Dedicated from a compliance perspective
05:20 Priya Singh: a couple of immediate actions: 1) we'll run a controlled load test in your staging with the same autoscaler settings and reproduce the spike, 2) we'll test client retry/backoff changes, 3) run a deduped trace capture to see if retries correlate to increased load
05:45 Mark Rivera: ok, one question on retry logic: what's Redwood's recommended default? our current client does 5 retries with linear backoff
06:00 Priya Singh: we recommend 3 retries max with exponential backoff starting at 200ms with jitter, and a per-route circuit-breaker for persistent 5xxs
06:18 Alex Kim: also want to note a pattern we saw: when KV cache evicts often on small instance sizes, tail latency spikes; so quantization settings and model chunking may help
06:35 Dana Liu: do you have any immediate mitigations we can apply before the live debugging session?
06:43 Priya Singh: yes - increase burst capacity in the autoscaler, enable short-term extra warm workers, add rate-limit guards on client, and adjust retry to recommended settings; we'll share a step-by-step runbook
07:02 Ellen Park: i'll gather ingress change logs and LB metrics and share before 2026-05-18
07:10 Mark Rivera: we'll also enable more verbose traces for that
07:18 Alex Kim: ok let's schedule the live debug, i'll propose 2026-05-20 09:00 PT in a calendar invite, Priya will lead the post-mortem debugging
07:25 Jamal Ortiz: i'll capture minutes and action items
07:30 Dana Liu: thanks all appreciate the quick response
07:33 Alex Kim: thanks everyone, recap in chat with links to benchmarks, SOC2, and the errors, and we'll close with next steps

[End of transcript]
